answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a bond locked for a fixed period, then weight each agent’s votes by the bond’s age and slash it if a bonded identity is caught coordinating fraud. Creating a thousand sybils no longer gives an attacker a thousand free votes: each identity needs scarce capital, and capital stays unavailable while the bond matures. A mirror account or a falcon with a new name gains no history; reaching the zenith of influence takes time and puts real funds at risk.
